title: Linearized gravity and gravitational-wave theory
scope: Gravity as a small perturbation of flat spacetime and the waves it supports, treated as theory: the metric perturbation and its Lorentz covariance, linearized curvature, linearized gauge transformations, trace reversal, the linearized Einstein equations and the Lorenz gauge, residual gauge freedom, the slow-motion ordering, the far field of stationary sources, gravitoelectromagnetism and the Lense-Thirring effect; plane waves, the transverse-traceless gauge, polarizations, the effect of waves on free test masses (strain and geodesic deviation); wave energy (flux, short-wave averaging, Isaacson tensor, angular momentum); generation by the retarded solution, multipoles, the quadrupole formula and luminosity, the absence of monopole and dipole radiation, circular binaries, radiation-driven inspiral and chirp mass; exact plane, impulsive, colliding and cylindrical waves; quasinormal modes of black holes as perturbation theory; Bondi-Sachs radiating spacetimes, news, Bondi mass loss and BMS symmetry; and the algebraic classification of curvature (principal null directions, Petrov types, optical scalars, peeling). Detectors, data analysis, sources and detections belong to gravitational-wave-astronomy; gravitons to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

concepts.title: Metric perturbation
concepts.summary: In a weak field one can pick coordinates where the metric is the Minkowski metric plus a small symmetric correction, g = eta + h with every |h| much less than 1; h carries all the gravitational information to first order, its indices are moved with eta, and its trace is h = eta^{mu nu} h_{mu nu}.

names: index raising with the background metric
index raising and lowering with the Minkowski metric

merged_from: index raising with the background metric
index raising and lowering with the Minkowski metric
concepts.notes: Fold-ins: the existence of nearly-Lorentz coordinates (even flat spacetime has coordinates that are not), the first-order inverse metric g^{mu nu} = eta^{mu nu} - h^{mu nu} (note the sign: the eta-raised h is minus the change of the inverse metric), the trace h, and the boundary condition h -> 0 far from sources. The GA ch47 weak-field-limit mention is this linearized convention; the Newtonian weak-field regime itself is owned by equivalence-principle.

concepts.title: Linearized gravity
concepts.summary: Linearized gravity keeps Einstein's equations only to first order in the metric perturbation h, turning general relativity into a linear tensor field theory on flat spacetime; it is valid when fields are weak everywhere in the region studied and is the setting for the Newtonian limit, gravitomagnetism and gravitational waves.
concepts.notes: Warn that linear superposition and the flat-background reading fail beyond first order; energy carried by waves needs second order (see short-wave-approximation).

concepts.title: Lorentz covariance of the metric perturbation
aliases: h as a tensor on Minkowski space
concepts.summary: Under a constant Lorentz transformation of the background coordinates eta is unchanged, so h transforms exactly like a rank-2 tensor of special relativity; this justifies treating weak gravity as a symmetric tensor field on flat spacetime, a bookkeeping picture that holds only for such transformations and to first order.

names: Lorentz covariance of the metric perturbation

merged_from: Lorentz covariance of the metric perturbation
concepts.notes: SCH and GA both label the flat-background view a useful fiction: the spacetime is really curved, and general (non-Lorentz) coordinate changes do not act on h as tensor transformations. The field-theory reading of gravity as a spin-2 field on flat space is owned by quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

concepts.title: Linearized Riemann tensor
concepts.summary: To first order in h the connection is Gamma^mu_{ab} = (1/2) eta^{mu nu}(h_{a nu,b} + h_{b nu,a} - h_{ab,nu}), products of connection coefficients drop out, and the Riemann tensor becomes a combination of four second derivatives of h: R_{a mu b nu} = (1/2)(h_{mu b,nu a} + h_{nu a,mu b} - h_{mu nu,ab} - h_{ab,mu nu}).

names: weak-field limit of the Riemann tensor

merged_from: weak-field limit of the Riemann tensor
concepts.notes: Examples folded in: the static weak-field case where R^i_{tjt} reduces to the Newtonian tidal tensor d_i d_j Phi (GA ch11, DIV ch10), and the TT-wave components R_{i0j0} = -(1/2) d_t^2 h_ij (GA ch46).

concepts.title: Gauge transformation of the metric perturbation
concepts.summary: A small coordinate shift x -> x + xi, with xi and its derivatives small, changes the perturbation by h_{mu nu} -> h_{mu nu} - xi_{mu,nu} - xi_{nu,mu} while describing the same spacetime; this redundancy is the gravitational analogue of A -> A - d chi in electromagnetism and can be spent to simplify the field equations.

names: gauge transformation of the metric perturbation
gauge transformation of the metric perturbation
gauge transformation of the metric perturbation

merged_from: gauge transformation of the metric perturbation
concepts.notes: SCH reinterprets the shift as an equivalence relation among perturbations on a fixed background rather than a relabelling of points. DIV ch10 uses slow-motion gauge vectors to show g_00 alone is gauge-invariant at that order. Only the GA ch46 gravitational use of the generic "gauge transformation" cluster is counted here; its electromagnetic mentions belong to electromagnetism-thermal-quantum.

concepts.title: Gauge invariance of linearized curvature
aliases: gauge invariance of the linearized Riemann tensor
concepts.summary: The first-order Riemann tensor, and hence its contractions, does not change under a linearized gauge transformation, because the added terms cancel pairwise as commuting partial derivatives of xi; curvature rather than h is therefore the physical content of a weak field.

names: gauge invariance of the linearized Riemann tensor
gauge invariance of the linearized Riemann tensor

merged_from: gauge invariance of the linearized Riemann tensor
concepts.notes: Used to evaluate curvature in TT gauge and read it in a local inertial frame (SCH ch09). SCH Exercise 8.5 links the calculation to Killing's equation.

concepts.title: Trace-reversed metric perturbation
concepts.summary: The combination h-bar_{mu nu} = h_{mu nu} - (1/2) eta_{mu nu} h has trace minus that of h, and applying the operation twice returns h; writing the linearized Einstein tensor in terms of h-bar removes the term in second derivatives of the trace and makes the field equations look like wave equations.
concepts.notes: In TT gauge h-bar and h coincide because the trace vanishes. DIV writes phi_ab and Phi_ab = epsilon phi_ab.

concepts.title: Linearized Einstein equations
concepts.summary: Contracting the linearized Riemann tensor gives first-order Ricci and Einstein tensors; in an arbitrary gauge the resulting equations read -box h-bar_{mu nu} - eta_{mu nu} h-bar^{ab}_{,ab} + h-bar_{mu a,nu}^{,a} + h-bar_{nu a,mu}^{,a} = 16 pi T_{mu nu} (G = c = 1), a linear system whose divergence terms can be removed by a gauge choice.
concepts.notes: GA ch14 and DIV ch12 quote the result early (already gauge fixed) to reach the Newtonian limit; full derivations are in SCH ch08, GA ch45 and DIV ch21. The linearized Einstein tensor is the trace reverse of the linearized Ricci tensor (SCH Exercise 8.8).

concepts.title: Lorenz gauge
concepts.summary: The Lorenz gauge imposes four conditions h-bar^{mu nu}_{,nu} = 0 on the trace-reversed perturbation (the gravitational twin of d_mu A^mu = 0); it can always be reached by solving box xi^mu = h-bar^{mu nu}_{,nu} for the gauge vector, and it collapses the linearized Einstein tensor to -(1/2) box h-bar_{mu nu}.
concepts.notes: The concept covers the electromagnetic condition as its template (GA ch42, DIV ch12) and the gravitational condition. "Lorentz gauge" is a common misattribution (L. V. Lorenz); in the full nonlinear theory the corresponding choice is harmonic coordinates, owned by einstein-field-equations.

concepts.title: Linearized field equations in Lorenz gauge
aliases: linearized Einstein equation in Lorenz gauge
concepts.summary: In Lorenz gauge the linearized Einstein equations become ten decoupled flat-space wave equations, box h-bar^{mu nu} = -16 pi T^{mu nu} (G = c = 1); their static limit gives Poisson's equation and their source-free solutions are gravitational waves travelling at the speed of light.

names: linearized Einstein equation in Lorenz gauge
linearized vacuum wave equation for hbar
linearized field equations as wave equations

merged_from: linearized Einstein equation in Lorenz gauge
linearized field equations as wave equations
linearized vacuum wave equation for hbar
concepts.notes: Signs depend on signature: DIV (+,-,-,-) writes box Phi_ab = -2 kappa T_ab. GA ch47 reaches the Fourier-space form h(k) proportional to (T - (1/2) eta T)/k^2 from field-theory counting; the graviton-propagator reading belongs to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

concepts.title: Residual gauge freedom
aliases: gauge freedom within the Lorenz class
concepts.summary: Imposing the Lorenz condition does not fix the gauge completely: any further shift generated by a vector obeying box xi = 0 preserves it, and for a plane wave choosing xi with the same wave vector supplies four free constants that can remove further components of the amplitude.

names: residual gauge transformation in linearized gravity

merged_from: residual gauge transformation in linearized gravity
concepts.notes: The electromagnetic version (shift by a function with box chi = 0, used to set A_0 = 0) is taught first in GA ch42 and DIV ch12 and is included as the template.

concepts.title: Slow-motion approximation
concepts.summary: For sources moving at speeds v much less than c, time derivatives are smaller than space derivatives by a factor of order v, so the d'Alembertian reduces to the Laplacian at leading order, and the stress-energy components are ordered T^00 >> T^0i >> T^ij (energy density, then momentum density ~ rho v, then stresses ~ rho v^2).
concepts.notes: SCH ch07 uses it in the geodesic equation (p^i << p^0) for the Newtonian limit; the source-size-versus-wavelength version used for radiation is long-wavelength-approximation. SCH notes exceptions: a rapidly rotating star can have T^0i larger than T^ij.

concepts.title: Far field of a stationary source
concepts.summary: Far from any isolated stationary source, the vacuum linearized equations in Lorenz gauge force the 1/r part of the field to be h-bar^00 = 4M/r only, so the metric approaches -(1 - 2M/r)dt^2 + (1 + 2M/r)(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2); this defines the mass M even for bodies with strong internal gravity.

names: far field of a stationary source

merged_from: far field of a stationary source
concepts.notes: SCH stresses that this far-field argument does not assume weak gravity inside the source, unlike the Newtonian-limit derivation.

concepts.title: Gravitoelectromagnetism
concepts.summary: For slowly moving sources, linearized gravity can be written like electromagnetism: the Newtonian potential acts as a scalar potential and h-bar_0i, sourced by mass currents, as a vector potential, giving gravitoelectric and gravitomagnetic fields that obey Maxwell-like equations with signs flipped because like masses attract.
concepts.notes: SCH Exercise 8.19: a rotating body's h-bar^0j falls as 1/r^2 and is proportional to its angular momentum, so prograde and retrograde orbits differ in period. Factor-of-2 and factor-of-4 conventions for the gravitomagnetic field vary between sources.

concepts.title: Lense-Thirring effect
concepts.summary: The gravitomagnetic field of a rotating mass drags nearby inertial frames: gyroscopes precess with an angular velocity of dipole form proportional to G/(c^2 r^3)[3(J.r-hat)r-hat - J], and satellite orbital planes precess; the effect has been measured around Earth by laser-ranged satellites and Gravity Probe B.
concepts.notes: The measurements (Gravity Probe B, LAGEOS) are owned by orbits-light-and-tests; frame dragging in Kerr is owned by black-holes. DIV uses the weak-field Lense-Thirring metric to identify ma with the Kerr angular momentum.

concepts.title: Gravitational wave
concepts.summary: A gravitational wave is a propagating ripple of spacetime curvature that travels at the speed of light, is produced by accelerating non-spherical mass-energy, and carries energy and angular momentum; in linearized theory it is a source-free solution of box h-bar = 0, and gauge-invariantly the linearized Riemann tensor itself obeys a wave equation.

names: Finite propagation speed of gravitational influence
wave equation for the Riemann tensor

merged_from: Finite propagation speed of gravitational influence
wave equation for the Riemann tensor
concepts.notes: DIV ch21 prefers box R_abcd = 0 (vacuum, Lorenz gauge) as the gauge-free argument that waves exist, adding that it does not by itself prove energy transport. DIV ch16 previews finite propagation speed against Newtonian instantaneous action.

concepts.title: Plane gravitational wave
concepts.summary: The plane-wave solution h-bar^{mu nu} = Re[A^{mu nu} exp(i k.x)] of the vacuum linearized equations requires a null wave vector (omega = |k|, no dispersion) and, from the Lorenz condition, an amplitude transverse to it, k_nu A^{mu nu} = 0; every vacuum solution is a superposition of such waves.
concepts.notes: DIV builds the wave as any function of t - x rather than a monochromatic ansatz. The dispersion relation omega^2 = |k|^2 (phase and group speed 1) is folded in here.

concepts.title: Transverse-traceless gauge
aliases: canonical form of a plane wave
concepts.summary: Spending the residual gauge freedom, a vacuum wave can be made traceless and orthogonal to a chosen observer's four-velocity as well as transverse; for propagation along z only h_xx = -h_yy and h_xy survive, h-bar equals h, and no gauge freedom remains, so these two components are physical.
concepts.notes: TT gauge exists only in vacuum regions; inside sources the Lorenz gauge is used and the field is projected afterwards (transverse-traceless-projection). The York transverse-traceless decomposition of initial data is a different construction owned by einstein-field-equations.

concepts.title: Gravitational-wave polarization
concepts.summary: A gravitational wave has two independent linear polarizations: plus, which stretches a ring of free particles along one transverse axis while squeezing it along the perpendicular one, and cross, the same pattern rotated by 45 degrees; any TT wave is h_+ e_+ + h_x e_x with basis tensors e_+ = e_x e_x - e_y e_y and e_x = e_x e_y + e_y e_x.

names: 45 degree polarization rotation and field rank

merged_from: 45 degree polarization rotation and field rank
concepts.notes: Key contrast: the two gravitational polarizations are 45 degrees apart (a spin-2 pattern repeats under 180-degree rotation; rotating the basis mixes h_+ and h_x at twice the angle), whereas electromagnetic ones are 90 degrees apart. Separations along the propagation direction are unaffected. Misconception: twenty Riemann components are not twenty polarizations. Helicity of the graviton is owned by quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

concepts.title: Circular and elliptical polarization of gravitational waves
concepts.summary: Complex combinations of the two linear states give circular polarization, h_xy = +/- i h_xx, in which the deformation ellipse rotates without changing shape, and elliptical polarization in general; a circular binary emits circularly polarized waves along its orbital axis and linearly polarized waves in its orbital plane, so the ellipticity encodes the inclination.

concepts.title: Free test masses in TT coordinates
aliases: geodesic motion of test masses in a gravitational wave
free particles remain at rest in TT gauge
concepts.summary: In TT gauge Gamma^i_00 vanishes, so a free particle initially at rest keeps constant spatial coordinates as a wave passes and TT time is its proper time; the coordinates are simply attached to free masses, so the wave's effect must be read from proper distances, light travel times or curvature, never from coordinate positions.

names: TT coordinates of free test masses
geodesic motion of test masses in a gravitational wave

merged_from: TT coordinates of free test masses
geodesic motion of test masses in a gravitational wave
concepts.notes: GA stages this as an apparent paradox (the wave seems to do nothing) to teach distrust of coordinate statements.

concepts.title: Gravitational-wave strain
aliases: proper distance in a gravitational-wave spacetime
concepts.summary: The proper distance between free masses a coordinate distance L apart along x oscillates as L(1 + h_+/2) to first order, and in general a mass at transverse offset x^j is displaced by (1/2) h^TT_ij x^j; the fractional change, of order h and at most about 1e-21 at Earth, grows with separation, which is why detectors are kilometres long.

names: proper distance in a gravitational-wave spacetime

merged_from: proper distance in a gravitational-wave spacetime
concepts.notes: Proper-distance strain is the invariant effect of the wave; detector response (return times, antenna patterns, noise) is owned by gravitational-wave-astronomy. Worked number (legacy): 4 km arms and h = 1e-21 give 2e-18 m per arm.

concepts.title: Geodesic deviation in a gravitational wave
aliases: tidal force of a gravitational wave
tidal acceleration of a gravitational wave
concepts.summary: In the local inertial frame of one free particle, the separation to a neighbour obeys d^2 xi^j/dt^2 = -R^j_{0k0} xi^k with R_{j0k0} = -(1/2) d_t^2 h^TT_jk, a transverse quadrupolar tidal field that reverses each half period; read as an effective force it adds to non-gravitational forces, which is why a rigid ruler barely stretches while free masses do.

names: geodesic deviation in a gravitational wave
tidal force of a gravitational wave
stretching of space and rigid rulers
transverse tidal acceleration in a plane wave

merged_from: geodesic deviation in a gravitational wave
tidal force of a gravitational wave
transverse tidal acceleration in a plane wave
stretching of space and rigid rulers
concepts.notes: Integrating twice from rest gives the displacement formula of gravitational-wave-strain. SCH answers the student question "why does a ruler not stretch if space does?": interatomic forces vastly exceed the wave's tidal force.

concepts.title: Geometrical optics for gravitational waves
concepts.summary: When a wave's wavelength and period are short compared with the curvature and change scales of the background, it travels along null geodesics and parallel-transports its polarization tensor, just like light, but it is almost unaffected by intervening matter because its coupling to matter is so weak.
concepts.notes: Stated qualitatively in SCH; lensing of gravitational waves follows from it.

concepts.title: Feynman sticky-bead argument
concepts.summary: Feynman's 1957 thought experiment: beads that slide with friction on a rod are moved by a passing wave's tidal field and heat the rod, so the wave must carry energy; it helped settle the debate over whether gravitational waves are physical.
concepts.notes: SCH turns it into a calculation with damped oscillators, whose properties drop out of the resulting flux formula.

concepts.title: Gravitational-wave energy flux
concepts.summary: A plane gravitational wave carries a period-averaged energy flux F = (1/32 pi) <(d_t h^TT_ij)(d_t h^TT_ij)>, which is omega^2 (A_+^2 + A_x^2)/32 pi for a monochromatic wave in G = c = 1 (c^3/16 pi G times <h_+dot^2 + h_x dot^2> in SI); it is meaningful only as an average and only in TT form.

names: energy flux of a gravitational wave

merged_from: energy flux of a gravitational wave
concepts.notes: SCH route: a sheet of oscillators absorbs energy and re-radiates downstream in antiphase, reducing the wave amplitude by exactly the absorbed amount (radiation reaction by destructive interference); energy conservation then fixes the flux. DIV route: heuristic from the quadratic Lagrangian, confirmed by the Isaacson tensor.

concepts.title: Short-wave approximation and averaging
concepts.summary: To give waves an energy, split the metric into a slowly varying background plus a small rapidly oscillating ripple, expand Einstein's equations to second order in the ripple, and average over regions several wavelengths across but smaller than the background curvature scale; under the average total derivatives vanish, removing gauge-dependent oscillating terms.
concepts.notes: At second order the linear operator acting on h^(2) is sourced by terms quadratic in h^(1) (DIV). GA motivates the split by comparing a detected strain of 1e-21 with Earth's static potential of about 1e-9.

concepts.title: Isaacson stress-energy tensor
aliases: effective energy-momentum tensor of gravitational waves
concepts.summary: Moving the averaged second-order part of the Einstein tensor to the source side defines an effective stress-energy for gravitational waves, T^GW_{mu nu} = (1/32 pi) <d_mu h^TT_ij d_nu h^TT ij> (G = c = 1); the average makes it gauge invariant, it sources the background curvature, and its T^0z component reproduces the plane-wave flux.

names: effective energy-momentum tensor of gravitational waves
effective energy-momentum tensor of gravitational waves

merged_from: effective energy-momentum tensor of gravitational waves
concepts.notes: Unaveraged, the pointwise second-order tensor is gauge dependent (a pseudotensor), consistent with the non-localizability of gravitational energy; averaging makes it quasi-local.

concepts.title: Lagrangian for linearized gravity
concepts.summary: Linearized general relativity follows from a Lagrangian density quadratic in first derivatives of h whose Euler-Lagrange equations reproduce the linearized Einstein tensor, showing that weak-field gravity is an ordinary field theory on flat space and suggesting that wave energy is quadratic in derivatives of h.
concepts.notes: DIV leaves the verification as an exercise; the book does not use the Fierz-Pauli name.

concepts.title: Retarded solution of the linearized field equations
concepts.summary: The causal solution of box h-bar_{mu nu} = -16 pi T_{mu nu} is h-bar_{mu nu}(t, x) = 4 integral T_{mu nu}(t - |x - y|, y)/|x - y| d^3y, an integral over the past light cone that keeps only outgoing waves; for a sinusoidal source outside it the leading solution is an outgoing spherical wave falling as 1/r.

names: retarded solution of the linearized field equation

merged_from: retarded solution of the linearized field equation
concepts.notes: Copied from electromagnetism with 16 pi G in place of 1. GA ch45 applies it to static dust to recover the weak-field metric, and to mass currents for gravitomagnetism. Retarded time t - |x - y|/c is folded in (GA ch46). The electromagnetic retarded potential and retarded time as first met in GA ch42 belong to electromagnetism-thermal-quantum (retarded-potential).

concepts.title: Far-zone approximation
concepts.summary: For an observer much farther from a compact source than the source's size, 1/|x - y| in the retarded integral is replaced by 1/r to the source centre, leaving a field that falls as 1/r; the region where this radiative 1/r part dominates is the wave zone, where the field looks locally like a plane wave.
concepts.notes: GA combines the far-zone and slow-motion simplifications in one step; DIV separates them (see long-wavelength-approximation).

concepts.title: Long-wavelength (slow-motion) approximation for radiation
concepts.summary: If the emitted wavelength is much larger than the source, equivalently if internal speeds are much less than c, retardation differences across the source can be ignored and every source element is evaluated at the same retarded time t - r; the leading radiation is then quadrupolar.
concepts.notes: This is SCH ch09's use of "slow-motion approximation" (the cluster's other uses are under slow-motion-approximation).

concepts.title: Mass and current multipole moments
concepts.summary: The far field of a bounded source can be expanded in multipoles weighted by moments of its mass density (I_l ~ M L^l) and of its mass current (S_l ~ M v L^l); current moments are suppressed by a factor v relative to mass moments of the same order, so for slow sources the time-varying field is dominated by the mass quadrupole.
concepts.notes: GA reviews the electromagnetic multipole expansion (antennas as oscillating dipoles) first.

concepts.title: Absence of monopole and dipole gravitational radiation
concepts.summary: Conservation of an isolated source's mass-energy, momentum and angular momentum fixes its monopole, mass dipole (centre of mass) and current dipole, so none can oscillate; gravitational radiation therefore starts at the quadrupole, unlike electromagnetism where the electric dipole radiates.

names: absence of monopole and dipole gravitational radiation
absence of monopole and dipole gravitational radiation

merged_from: absence of monopole and dipole gravitational radiation
concepts.notes: Legacy check question: a mass dipole cannot radiate because momentum is conserved.

concepts.title: Mass quadrupole moment tensor
concepts.summary: The second moment of the mass-energy distribution, I^{jk}(t) = integral T^00 x^j x^k d^3x, is the source quantity whose second time derivative sets the leading gravitational wave field of a slow source.

names: second mass moment and reduced quadrupole moment

merged_from: second mass moment and reduced quadrupole moment
concepts.notes: Convention trap: SCH and DIV define I without removing the trace and without a factor of 3 (MTW convention), unlike the electrostatic quadrupole; GA calls it the moment of inertia tensor although it differs from the rigid-body inertia tensor.

concepts.title: Tensor virial identity
concepts.summary: For a compact source with conserved stress-energy (d_nu T^{mu nu} = 0 in linearized theory), the volume integral of the stresses equals half the second time derivative of the mass quadrupole: integral T^{jk} d^3x = (1/2) d^2/dt^2 integral T^00 x^j x^k d^3x.
concepts.notes: Proof: differentiate the energy continuity equation in time, use momentum conservation to get a double divergence, and integrate by parts twice. DIV notes that for self-gravitating binaries flat-space conservation must be qualified.

concepts.title: Reduced (trace-free) quadrupole moment
concepts.summary: The trace-free part of the mass quadrupole, I-bar_jk = I_jk - (1/3) delta_jk I^l_l; the TT wave field and the radiated power depend only on it, so a spherically symmetric mass distribution, whose quadrupole is proportional to delta_jk, contributes nothing.

names: second mass moment and reduced quadrupole moment

concepts.notes: Legacy pitfall: removing the three-dimensional trace uses 1/3, while TT projection removes a two-dimensional transverse trace with 1/2.

concepts.title: Quadrupole formula
concepts.summary: Far from a slowly moving compact source the wave field is h-bar_jk = (2/r) d^2 I_jk/dt^2 evaluated at retarded time t - r (2G/(c^4 r) in SI), obtained from the far-zone retarded integral of T_jk by using the tensor virial identity.

names: quadrupole formula for the wave field

merged_from: quadrupole formula for the wave field
concepts.notes: Sign conventions differ (DIV writes Phi_ij = -(2/r) d^2 I_ij/dt^2 with signature +---). SCH justifies applying it to Newtonian-gravity-bound sources only by citing the literature.

concepts.title: Transverse-traceless projection
concepts.summary: To extract the radiative part of a field propagating along unit vector n, project a symmetric tensor onto the transverse plane with P_ij = delta_ij - n_i n_j and subtract half its transverse trace: X^TT_ij = (P_ik P_jl - (1/2) P_ij P_kl) X_kl.
concepts.notes: For n along z it gives h_xx^TT = (h-bar_xx - h-bar_yy)/2 and h_xy^TT = h-bar_xy.

concepts.title: Quadrupole luminosity formula
concepts.summary: The total power radiated by a slow-motion source is L = (G/5c^5) <d^3 I-bar_jk/dt^3 d^3 I-bar^jk/dt^3>, found by integrating the TT energy flux over a large sphere; the tiny prefactor G/5c^5 means only compact, rapidly moving astrophysical masses radiate appreciably.

names: energy flux through a distant sphere

merged_from: energy flux through a distant sphere
concepts.notes: The angular integrals use the isotropic averages of n^i n^j and n^i n^j n^k n^l. A source with a time-independent quadrupole (steadily rotating axisymmetric body) emits no quadrupole radiation.

concepts.title: Angular momentum carried by gravitational waves
concepts.summary: Gravitational waves remove angular momentum at the rate dJ_i/dt = -(2G/5c^5) epsilon_ijk <d^2 I-bar_jl/dt^2 d^3 I-bar_kl/dt^3>; an axisymmetric source loses none, and for a circular binary the loss matches the orbital energy-angular momentum relation.

names: angular momentum carried by gravitational waves

merged_from: angular momentum carried by gravitational waves
concepts.notes: GA quotes the result from Maggiore; SCH Exercise 9.54 obtains angular-momentum loss from the Isaacson tensor.

concepts.title: No gravitational radiation from spherical motion
concepts.summary: A source that pulsates, collapses or explodes while remaining spherically symmetric emits no gravitational waves at any order, because Birkhoff's theorem fixes its exterior as static Schwarzschild; in the quadrupole picture its trace-free quadrupole vanishes.

names: no gravitational radiation from spherically symmetric motion

merged_from: no gravitational radiation from spherically symmetric motion
concepts.notes: SCH warns that a leading-order argument is not a proof: a rotating square of four equal masses has constant quadrupole yet radiates at higher order. Legacy check: spherical breathing does not radiate.

concepts.title: Gravitational waves from a circular binary
concepts.summary: Applying the quadrupole formula to two masses in a Newtonian circular orbit gives waves at twice the orbital frequency with amplitude falling as 1/r, radiation pattern proportional to (1 + cos^2 theta) for h_+ and 2 cos theta for h_x, and total power 32 G^4 m1^2 m2^2 (m1 + m2)/(5 c^5 a^5).

names: frequency doubling of binary gravitational waves
angular distribution of binary gravitational radiation
quadrupole luminosity of a circular binary

merged_from: frequency doubling of binary gravitational waves
angular distribution of binary gravitational radiation
quadrupole luminosity of a circular binary
concepts.notes: Frequency doubling: the mass distribution returns to itself after half an orbit. Power is strongest along the orbital axis (circular polarization) and weakest in the orbital plane (pure plus). For equal masses m at radius R, L = (128/5) m^2 R^4 Omega^6 (G = c = 1).

concepts.title: Radiation-driven binary inspiral
aliases: binary inspiral driven by gravitational radiation
concepts.summary: A bound binary losing energy to gravitational waves becomes more tightly bound, so its separation and period shrink and its orbital speed, wave frequency and amplitude all rise until merger; balancing the Newtonian orbital energy E = -G m1 m2/(2a) against the quadrupole luminosity gives the rate, with df/dt proportional to f^(11/3).

names: binary inspiral driven by gravitational radiation
binding energy of a circular binary

merged_from: binary inspiral driven by gravitational radiation
binding energy of a circular binary
concepts.notes: Paradox worth teaching: losing energy speeds the binary up (negative specific heat of bound orbits). Measured period decay of binary pulsars and observed chirp signals (GW150914) belong to gravitational-wave-astronomy; GA and DIV note that the Newtonian and linear approximations fail near merger.

concepts.title: Chirp mass
concepts.summary: The chirp mass (m1 m2)^(3/5)/(m1 + m2)^(1/5) is the only combination of a binary's masses that enters the leading-order waveform amplitude, luminosity and frequency evolution, so it can be read directly from f and df/dt and is the best-measured parameter of an inspiral.

names: remaining orbital phase and mass-independent luminosity

merged_from: remaining orbital phase and mass-independent luminosity
concepts.notes: Folded-in SCH result (Forward-Berman): the orbital phase left before merger is (1/32)(M_chirp omega)^(-5/3), so a circular binary's luminosity L = 1/(160 psi^2) depends only on how many orbits remain, whatever its masses. Time-to-merger and scale-free scaling laws used in observation belong to gravitational-wave-astronomy.

concepts.title: Exact plane gravitational wave
aliases: Rosen form of a plane wave
concepts.summary: Einstein's equations admit exact vacuum plane waves, for example ds^2 = -du dv + f(u)^2 dx^2 + g(u)^2 dy^2 with u = t - z, whose only field equation is f''/f + g''/g = 0; one profile function can be chosen freely, small amplitudes reproduce the linear plus-polarized wave, and all scalar curvature invariants vanish although the Riemann tensor does not.

names: linearly polarized exact plane gravitational wave
Rosen form of a plane wave

merged_from: linearly polarized exact plane gravitational wave
Rosen form of a plane wave
concepts.notes: In Rosen form free particles sit at constant transverse coordinates, but the coordinates become singular at focusing (fold) points. DIV writes h = f''/f = -g''/g for the profile.

concepts.title: Brinkmann form of a plane wave
concepts.summary: In Brinkmann coordinates a plane wave reads h(U)(Z^2 - Y^2) dU^2 + dU dV - dY^2 - dZ^2: flat space plus one term quadratic in the transverse coordinates with the profile explicit, so co-propagating waves superpose exactly by adding profiles and do not scatter each other.

names: Brinkmann form of a plane wave
exact superposition of co-propagating plane waves

concepts.title: Sandwich wave
concepts.summary: A sandwich wave is an exact plane wave whose curvature is confined to a slab between two parallel null hypersurfaces, with flat spacetime before and after; a geodesic observer crossing it feels a transient transverse tidal acceleration.

concepts.title: Impulsive plane gravitational wave
concepts.summary: An impulsive plane wave is the thin-slab limit of a sandwich wave: flat spacetime on both sides of a single null hypersurface carrying delta-function curvature, given in Rosen form by f = 1 + u theta(u), g = 1 - u theta(u) and in Brinkmann form by h = delta(U).

concepts.title: Colliding plane gravitational waves
concepts.summary: Because Einstein's equations are nonlinear, two counter-propagating plane waves do not simply pass through each other: in the region where both are present the metric depends on both null coordinates and the waves scatter and focus one another, typically producing a singularity.
concepts.notes: Details folded in: any oblique collision can be boosted to head-on; the interaction region lies to the future of both wavefronts; Szekeres' general form has four functions M, U, V, W of (u, v), with W = 0 for parallel polarizations; step waves (finite curvature jumps) appear after collision.

concepts.title: Khan-Penrose solution
concepts.summary: The Khan-Penrose solution describes two colliding linearly polarized impulsive plane waves exactly: flat regions before the collision, and a curved interaction region that ends in a spacelike curvature singularity, with fold singularities along its edges.
concepts.notes: Singularity at u^2 + v^2 = 1 in DIV's coordinates.

concepts.title: Einstein-Rosen cylindrical waves
concepts.summary: For whole-cylinder symmetry the metric reduces to e^{2 gamma - 2 psi}(dt^2 - d rho^2) - rho^2 e^{-2 psi} d phi^2 - e^{2 psi} dz^2, and the vacuum equations become the ordinary linear flat-space cylindrical wave equation for psi, with gamma then fixed by line integration; regular pulses such as the Weber-Wheeler solution implode and re-expand and carry energy.
concepts.notes: Historical note: Einstein and Rosen first took the singular behaviour of such waves as evidence against gravitational waves; the regular Weber-Wheeler pulse (J0 modes with exponential weighting) refuted that worry. Integrability of gamma holds exactly when psi obeys the wave equation.

concepts.title: Quasinormal modes
concepts.summary: A perturbed black hole settles to a stationary Kerr state by emitting gravitational waves in damped characteristic oscillations whose frequencies and damping times depend only on the final mass and spin; they die away within a few cycles, much faster than stellar oscillation modes.
concepts.notes: Theory owned here per taxonomy; the observed ringdown signal and spectroscopy tests are owned by gravitational-wave-astronomy. Matching the measured spectrum to Kerr tests the identity of a merger remnant.

concepts.title: Bondi-Sachs radiation coordinates
concepts.summary: Radiation coordinates are adapted to outgoing null cones: retarded time u labels the null hypersurfaces, r runs along each null ray and is chosen so that the u, r = const two-surfaces have area 4 pi r^2, and the angles label rays by where they reach future null infinity.
concepts.notes: Bondi's areal choice of r is an alternative to the Newman-Penrose affine parameter.

concepts.title: Bondi-Sachs radiating metric
concepts.summary: The general axisymmetric, non-rotating metric in radiation coordinates has four free functions V, U, beta, gamma of (u, r, theta); demanding asymptotic flatness and no incoming radiation and expanding in 1/r (for example gamma = n/r + q/r^3 + ..., V = r - 2M + ...) organizes the solution by a few functions of retarded time and angle.
concepts.notes: Bondi's outgoing radiation condition, modelled on the Sommerfeld condition, turns out not to exclude sufficiently weak incoming radiation. Sachs extended the metric beyond axisymmetry.

concepts.title: Bondi hierarchy of the field equations
concepts.summary: Bondi sorted the vacuum equations for his metric into hypersurface equations that fix beta, U and V along each null cone once gamma is known, one evolution equation giving gamma's retarded-time derivative, one trivial equation and supplementary conditions that need hold only at one radius; this yields a marching scheme from null cone to null cone.
concepts.notes: The Bianchi identities justify why the supplementary equations propagate.

concepts.title: Bondi news function
concepts.summary: The news function is the retarded-time derivative of the 1/r coefficient of gamma; it is the free data at null infinity that drives the evolution, vanishes exactly when no radiation is emitted, and without axial symmetry comes as two functions, one per polarization.

concepts.title: Bondi mass
concepts.summary: The Bondi mass is the total mass-energy of an isolated system measured on a cut of future null infinity, the angular average of the mass aspect M(u, theta) in V = r - 2M + ...; it agrees with the ADM and Komar masses when the system is stationary, and it is non-negative when the dominant energy condition holds.
concepts.notes: The dipole and quadrupole aspects are the r^-3 coefficients in U and gamma, reducing to Newtonian moments in static weak fields. Positivity is credited to Ludvigsen and Vickers (1981).

concepts.title: Bondi mass-loss formula
concepts.summary: For an asymptotically flat isolated system the Bondi mass obeys dm/du = -(1/2) integral (n_,u)^2 sin theta d theta <= 0, so the mass is constant exactly when there is no news and strictly decreases otherwise; this proves without any weak-field approximation that gravitational radiation carries away mass-energy.
concepts.notes: DIV frames the chapter around a bounded source that is stationary, radiates for a while, and settles to a smaller mass, making energy transport rather than the mere existence of wave solutions the test of whether gravitational radiation is real.

concepts.title: Bondi-Metzner-Sachs group
concepts.summary: The BMS group consists of the coordinate transformations that preserve the Bondi form of an asymptotically flat metric and its fall-off; it is the asymptotic symmetry group of radiating isolated systems, larger than the Poincare group because it contains angle-dependent translations called supertranslations.
concepts.notes: DIV only mentions it; supertranslations are standard context not developed in the book.

concepts.title: Principal null directions
concepts.summary: Where the Weyl tensor is nonzero, the null vectors l satisfying l_[a C_b]ef[c l_d] l^e l^f = 0 define between one and four principal null directions at each point, and the pattern in which they coincide characterizes the algebraic type of the gravitational field.
concepts.notes: Principal null congruences of Kerr (DIV ch20) are handled by curvature/black-holes.

concepts.title: Petrov classification
concepts.summary: The Petrov classification sorts the Weyl tensor at a point by coincidences of its principal null directions: type I (four distinct), II (one pair coincides), D (two pairs), III (three coincide), N (all four) and O (Weyl tensor zero); spacetimes other than type I are algebraically special, and types can only become more special along the arrows of Penrose's diagram.
concepts.notes: Misconceptions from the dossier: realistic radiating spacetimes are type I (only their 1/r part is type N); Kerr, Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordstrom are all type D. Eigenvector counts in tables depend on the matrix formalism; teach via PND multiplicities. The Plebanski classification of the trace-free Ricci tensor is only mentioned.

concepts.title: Tidal signatures of Petrov types
concepts.summary: Szekeres read each Petrov type through the relative accelerations of a sphere of free particles: type N distorts only transverse to the propagation direction like a linear wave, type III adds a distortion tilted in a plane containing that direction, and type D stretches along one axis and squeezes the two perpendicular ones like the tides of a static mass.
concepts.notes: Types I and II give no simple picture.

concepts.title: Optical scalars of a null congruence
concepts.summary: For an affinely parametrized null geodesic congruence, the expansion, twist and shear built from the covariant derivative of its tangent describe how a small cross-section of the beam grows, rotates and distorts along the rays; Sachs showed they are the enlargement, rotation and shearing of a shadow cast on a nearby screen, the same for every screen velocity.
concepts.notes: Shear is singled out because of the Goldberg-Sachs theorem (owned by black-holes) and its link to news; twist vanishes for hypersurface-orthogonal congruences such as the generators of u = const.

concepts.title: Newman-Penrose formalism
concepts.summary: The Newman-Penrose formalism writes all geometric quantities as components along a null tetrad of two real and two complex null vectors, packaging the Weyl tensor into five complex scalars; it is the standard language for radiation, peeling and exact-solution work.
concepts.notes: Only mentioned in DIV; the tetrad itself is owned by differential-forms-and-frames.

concepts.title: Peeling theorem
concepts.summary: Along an outgoing null ray in an asymptotically flat radiating spacetime the curvature falls off as N/r + III/r^2 + II/r^3 + I/r^4, each term having the ray as a principal null direction of decreasing multiplicity; far away the field is type N, a local plane wave, and the principal null directions separate as one moves inward.
concepts.notes: Stated first for Sachs' linearized retarded waves, then for isolated systems.

concepts.title: Goldberg-Sachs theorem
concepts.summary: In vacuum, the Weyl tensor has a repeated principal null direction exactly when the spacetime admits a shear-free congruence of null geodesics running along that direction. It links the algebraic Petrov type of the curvature to the geometry of light rays, and underlies the Kerr principal null congruences.
